transcript:
This message comes from Capital One with the Capital One Saver Card.
Earn unlimited 3% cash back on dining and entertainment.
Capital One. What's in your wallet? Terms apply. Details at CapitalOne.com.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dan Ronan.
Democrats are turning to online influencers to win a lost electorate.
Latino voters who are frustrated with both parties.
NPR's Claudia Grisales reports House Democrats
are kicking off a national tour today with content creators in several swing districts.
The campaign arm of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus is fighting for Latino
voters who deserted Democrats in the 2024 elections, having come back.
California Democratic Congresswoman Linda Sanchez, who chairs the group,
says they're asking content creators for help to bridge the gap.
We're turning to trusted voices in local communities that have following,
giving them information and then allowing them to create content in a way that is organic and authentic.
Latinos get their political news from influencers more than any other demographic.
Content creators will join Get Out the Vote events in Colorado,
Florida, New Mexico, Texas, and Arizona.
Claudia Grisales, NPR News.
Mexico's west coast is being pounded by a category four hurricane.
NPR's Idra Peralta reports it's forecast to bring torrential rain and dangerous winds.
The good news is that Hurricane Simon is expected to skirt the coast and will likely not directly
hit the bigger cities along its path. Still, Colima and Puerto Vallarta are reporting strong
winds, heavy surf, and flooding. Mexican President Claudia Shambam has ordered citizens in four
different municipalities to shelter in place until the danger has passed.
Shambam has also deployed the military in those areas to help with recovery.
The National Hurricane Center expects Hurricane Simon to weaken in the coming hours and then
continue moving along the coast. Simon is forecast to make landfall on Wednesday near Masatlan.
Forecasters say it will likely be a tropical storm by then.
Idra Peralta, NPR News, Mexico City.
The fourth winter in Gaza since the war began is approaching,
and humanitarian groups say Israeli restrictions on shelter supplies are leaving Palestinians
exposed to cold weather and flooding. NPR's Anis Baba reports from Gaza.
The aid group, the Norwegian Refugee Council,
says 500 truckloads of shelter items are ready to enter Gaza.
But at current Israeli entry rates, it will take until next summer to bring them in.
Israel says it has facilitated the entry of tents, blankets, and winter clothes.
Its military, however, says it has banned shelter kits that have wooden poles,
arguing Hamas could use them. The U.N. Migration Agency says nearly
two million people in Gaza need shelter assistance and that the agency has more than
8,500 shelter kits ready for delivery, but that Israel is blocking these supplies at crossings.
Palestinians say tents are not a way to live, and aid groups warn
a million people are at high risk of flooding.
It's NPR.
Pope Leo will undergo surgery this week to remove a small growth on his lung.
Megan Williams reports that doctors found the nodule during a routine checkup.
Pope Leo told pilgrims gathered in St. Peter's Square on Sunday that doctors had found what he
called a localized nodule in his lung. He said it was detected at a very early stage and is well
contained, but doctors recommended removing it. The Vatican says the surgery will take place in
the coming days, with Leo expected to recover in about a week. It's the first known health
scare for the American Pope since his election last year. Leo is physically active and plays
tennis regularly. Next month he's due to make a 12-day trip to Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru,
where he lived for two decades and holds citizenship. The Vatican has not said whether
the surgery will affect those plans. For NPR News, I'm Megan Williams in Rome.
A bipartisan group of seven US senators, four Republicans and three Democrats,
are now calling on President Trump to immediately reverse his course on a plan to purchase diesel
from Russia. Trump made the announcement last week in an effort to lower the price of diesel,
which hit a record high last month of more than $6.50 a gallon, before declining slightly to
$6.27 a gallon today, according to AAA. The senators said the White House failed to consult
with Congress or provide any explanation for that action, which they say is required by law.
They say it also provides a financial lifeline to Russia. I'm Dan Ronan, NPR News, Washington.

topics.text: Democrats tour swing districts with online influencers to win back Latino voters before elections
Hurricane Simon strengthens to Category 4 off Mexico's west coast; Colima and Puerto Vallarta hit by winds
Israeli restrictions on shelter supplies leave Gaza's Palestinians exposed to winter cold and flooding
Pope Leo to undergo surgery this week to remove small, early-stage nodule from his lung
Seven bipartisan senators urge Trump to reverse plan to buy diesel from Russia, citing lack of consultation
